utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par, we were informed that you are going to address the Chamber before we have the next witness. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I will try to be brief. I would like to request leave for addressing the Chamber before we continue with the normal session with a question regarding the scope of examination-in-chief of this witness. I would again request the position of the Chamber regarding the examination of this witness about things which are not within the scope of the indictment because according to the statement of this witness that we have been given, it follows that he spoke about certain things beyond the scope of the indictment. I do not know if he has the right to be asked about these things, and I don't know if I will have time to put in my objection. I don't know how long or to what extent the Prosecutor intends to question him about such issues. My question is: Is it the position of the Trial Chamber that they would allow for this witness to be questioned about things which are not covered by the indictment during the examination-in-chief, although this witness has had knowledge about these things for a number of years? The position of the Defence of Vinko Martinovic is that the Prosecutor should not be allowed to introduce unverified stories that he himself did not want to include in the indictment and that could leave the wrong impression about the accused. We believe it is wrong to charge the accused with some things in the indictment and then talk about completely different things during examination-in-chief. We believe that this witness should be questioned in accordance with the indictment and that the judgment should also be made accordingly. This is the practice that we are familiar with, that we adhere to, and we would like to hear the opinion of the Chamber as to whether we are right and whether this position can be upheld in this court as well, and to instruct us otherwise if the Chamber believes that is necessary. That is all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you allow me to say a couple of more things in the same context, especially since we have the next witness pending today. I have received the Prosecutor's request for closed session for the examination of that lady witness. The charge is that she was raped. And from the very request, we can see that the Prosecutor intends to examine her on something that is not in the indictment. That same victim of rape is now supposed to be subjected to both examination-in-chief and cross-examination regarding a crime that was not included in the indictment. So the situation is similar to the one that was discussed by my colleague, Mr. Par. I have nothing against the protective measures proposed for this witness, but I just want to say that I believe that it is not necessary to examine her at all, because this crime is not among the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honour, I hadn't thought I would need to be on my feet again for the same reason, because we are dealing here with a cross-examination of a protected witness, whose identity I allegedly revealed. This lady witness mentioned by my colleague Mr. Seric says that on television - I don't know which television or where - she saw me divulging her identity, and that is one more reason why she needs protective measures. Your Honours, I have to say that after we cross-examined the protected witness and after we studied the transcript, it must be clear that I did not reveal her identity, that the name mentioned is completely different, and I think it can be confirmed. So after we have clarified this, I was corrected and I apologised, and for the Prosecutor to raise this issue again in such an improper way is really unexpected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess Mr. Meek will not take the floor this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning. Very briefly, early on in this trial, the Trial Chamber asked that both sides talked to each other before we filed any motions. I have endeavoured to speak with the Prosecutors whenever possible before I filed a motion. This motion that we received today about the lady who will be coming on next was unexpected because they did not talk with us. Had they talked with us, we probably could have resolved this very briefly and shortly. That's all I would have to say, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So Mr. Scott is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to make address the general issue. And concerning in particular the next witness, who Mr. Stringer will be handling, in terms of the particular items of that witness, I will turn to Mr. Stringer on. As the more general matter for the trial as a whole on this topic, Mr. President, Your Honours, this seems to be become a new tactic over the past couple of weeks, probably prompted by the recent ruling in the Kupreskic appeal. And I've seen this happen, of course, as we probably all have, in our own jurisdictions before: A new case comes out, particularly an appellate case, that is widely read in a particular community, and then that becomes the common topic of -- in all hearings and cases for some weeks and months thereafter as every Defence team, or every Prosecution team, for that matter, raises that issue du jour, if I can put it that way. That is not what is happening in this case. It's not a situation where the Prosecution here is attempting by any means to substitute "new charges" for charges not in the indictment. This is simply a matter of evidence. It is simply a matter of evidence that goes to what is in fact charged in the indictment. Indictments do not have to - and I submit not even under any current or new ICTY jurisprudence - have to plead the details of the evidence that a party will submit to support particular charges. Both of these accused are charged with courses of conduct involving the repeated expulsions of families and civilians and others from homes in Mostar. They are charged with a course of conduct by their own conduct and by instigation and by their example to their subordinates, the beating and mistreatment of prisoners, the use of prisoners for forced labour, the use of prisoners as human shields, et cetera. Now, it's clear that not every single incident, not every single name of every prisoner so victimised, of every Muslim family so victimised, is named in the indictment. And we suggest -- we take the position that that is not required. But the charges being what they are, the Prosecution, we submit, is entitled to present its case, is entitled to present the witnesses' testimony and evidence on these matters. Now, again, I'm going to let Mr. Stringer address specifically the testimony of this next witness - not the one we are in the middle of now but the next witness - and that probably should be done in private session because it touches on a protected witness matter. There was also -- before I forget it, there was also a reference just now by one of the counsel, that this also had something to do with -- is based on reports by others. Well, this Chamber knows well by now that hearsay is widely accepted in this Chamber. Clearly there may become -- in this institution, excuse me. Clearly there may come an instance, there may be circumstances where the hearsay becomes so remote that it should not be heard. That is not this case. This hearsay is no different than the hearsay that is admitted in the three courtrooms of this institution every day. So that simply is not a basis to exclude this evidence. Your Honour, the witnesses come and they tell their whole story. It is completely artificial, in our view, to have a witness come, for instance, that has been expelled from her home and not be able to tell her full story and act as if certain things didn't happen during the time that her and her family were expelled. It is simply saying, "Well, we're not going to let you tell us about that." It is directly relevant to the charges in the indictment. There is no attempt by the Prosecution to substitute any new or different charges. The charges are what they are, and this evidence is directly relevant to that. And further, there is no surprise here. There has been -- the notice has been given a long time ago, either in the indictment as to what the charges are, and in all the 65 ter summaries that the Prosecution has made. These summaries of witness testimony, what we expected the witnesses to testify, were made over a year ago in the original 65 ter summaries back when the Chamber was comprised among the other Judges. 65 ter summaries were provided at that time. This testimony was included. The Defence has had notice of this for over a year. So this is not a surprise issue. It is not properly a hearsay issue. It is not properly a question of changing the charges in the indictment. It is simply a matter of the Chamber hearing evidence from witnesses who have come a long way to tell their stories and on evidence on which the Defence has had notice for more than a year. We completely oppose, obviously, the Defence position on this. The Chamber should hear this evidence, and I leave it to Mr. Stringer to address the more details of that particular witness in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please remember that you are still under the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Knudsen, yesterday our session was adjourned at the moment when we were discussing the confrontation line. My question will be: Was Vinko Skrobo the only unit that was in charge of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were there any other units who were involved in guarding the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told we had a unit on our right side who were supposed to be a Kaznjenicka Bojna as well, and I'm not sure if it's true, but we were supposed to have Vojna Policija, military police, on our left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit Number 14.4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You want it to be annoted? I would like to give the number now, P14.4/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Knudsen, what does this picture depict?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What does this picture depict?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture is our positions. If you look at the big white building, we would have a position at the corner of it. And we had this large building here. We didn't have anything in that. Here, we had this big red building which was a bunker on the side of it so you could watch in the gar [phoen] here. And down here, there is what you call a command bunker. And over here, this one, we had a position as well at the corner of the house. And it would go in a shift, one, two, three, four, and five positions. You got the confrontation line going here. This side is the Croatian side. And where the line did go from there, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Let's stop at this point. And it would be appropriate if we mark all these positions in this picture. Please take a marker. So with a number "1," I invite you to mark your first position in the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: With number "2," I invite you to mark the position on this long building, multi-storey building with a red roof.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could I have a look? Put it on the ELMO just to check if -- yes, yes, yes. I mean on the left side. The building on the left side should be marked with number "2."

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And then you mentioned a third building that had some positions and a sort of basement?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you mark it on this picture.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't see number "3." Where is it? Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point it out? This is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, because you have a green marker, and you put your mark on the green colour.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But it's okay. Witness, when you say that you had your position, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean is that you make, like, a shift, which means if you came on the first day, you would stay at position 1, and this would be your guard line that day. And then you have 12 hours off at a time, and a certain time we had 25 hours off. And then next time you come -- can I mark something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What did you --

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote "4" there because in the yard - there is a yard behind - we had also a position, so you can be on the lookout here. And then we go like this, that one day you would be sitting on one position, next day you came, you will be sitting on the next position, and you would go around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Let's now go to your position indicated as number "2." In which part of the building exactly did you have your positions?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had it at the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Of the ground floor or on the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what was there in the other parts of the building?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, like, just apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were they vacant or occupied by the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would guess one or two lived at the front line; people did that down there. But otherwise, I wouldn't say that anybody lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you ever have your shifts in the building number 3?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a corner with sandbags, where you would sit behind and just listen with your back against the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Knudsen, I would like to hear from you. For example, you are in position number 2.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Which part of the confrontation line was supposed to be under your control?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This yard here. It was actually all about, I would say, position 4, and position 3 were only about to guard this yard here because the Muslims could get in here at that time. Position number 2, you were supposed to be on the watchout for this piece here, because at a frequent time, you had a bunker system built in here, the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what about position 1?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Position 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What was the area of your observation?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Position 1 was also at the corner. It was built up like you were sitting in a chair, with your back against the line, and you had this mirror on your left side. So you watched in the mirror, and you could see what was happening, and it was the same thing again. You were watching this piece here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And you just told the Trial Chamber that there was a sort of basement in your position number 3?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And for what purposes was that basement used?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose that -- in number 3, you had the end of the building. Down the basement, I would have what we say like a command bunker, I guess. It's not really a bunker. It's sandbag built in. And then would you go down the basement, you had what we call a sort of trenches or built like trenches, that run along the building to got up in the end of the building here, so you could go to position 1, 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And you also said that there were some other units just involved in the guarding of the confrontation line. Could you show in this picture the locations that were under those units' control?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can put it like this: These buildings here were in control of our unit. And how exactly the line went at that time down here, we didn't actually know. But we were asking once who were in command or who was on our right side here, and were told it was another Kaznjenicka Bojna. And then we asked who was on our left side, and we didn't go there, but we were told that it was military police guarding this piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And could you just indicate where the enemy positions were?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines was going here, as we knew, and up here then, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So just to clarify, there are two destroyed buildings?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, these destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, and the next one, upper.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps with numbers "5" and "6," you should indicate those two buildings. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: According to today's testimony, there was a sort of command office in your position number 3. Did you ever see Stela in that bunker?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the bunker?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was later on, not in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see any other commanders in that bunker?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw other officers at the bunker. What I mean is we didn't talk to these people. But you got insignia, or your having a Motorola. You were an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Would you tell the Trial Chamber how many of Stela's subordinates you can identify as his commanders, sub-commanders, let's say? Do you remember anyone?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only remember Alan as we was thinking about one of the subordinate officers. But this is this guy I know by name. Other guys I've seen, I can only tell by viewing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So if I correctly understand you, the main, just criteria was if the soldier had a Motorola and some insignia?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Motorola or some insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Were those buildings in your area of responsibility somehow fortified?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were fortified with sandbags from the inside. Excuse me, can I remove this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And who was in charge of making or repairing of those fortifications?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prisoners were. We had prisoners working at the front line all the time. And if something happened, these guys would build it up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And where did you take those prisoners from?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I guess they were taken from Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Heliodrom to pick up prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think about two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And did they return prisoners normally on the same day to Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what do you know was happening to the prisoners taken from Heliodrom? Where did they keep them?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not exactly sure where they kept them because the only times we see them under guard off line, they would be in, like, a small glass house, those ones in which you sell papers, cigarettes, standing next to Stela's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And how did Stela and his subordinates treat prisoners who were involved in some jobs on the Bulevar or were kept in other places or Stela's responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. What do you mean by the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Treated. It's a very broad term. It's a broad term.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was their treatment, let's say, humane?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean if I saw any torture or beatings, no, I did not see that done by Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you know of any facts of prisoners being mistreated by other members of the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone actually get beaten by someone in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But were you informed of any facts of beating? Did you have any knowledge of such kind of facts?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly, no. I wouldn't say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And just about foreign soldiers, how did they treat prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean generally, or do you mean a specific incidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Generally and specific incidents.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally they were treated all right. We didn't have a lot of contact. What I mean is you go to the line, and you got prisoners working. These prisoners would bring coffee or build up sandbags or removing sandbags. You were not supposed to sit down and talk to these guys, so therefore we didn't have much contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Apart from your daily duties, which consisted in guarding the confrontation line, were Stela's soldiers involved in some other jobs which were carried out not within the area indicated by you, just in the picture? Did they go to perform any duties to some other parts of Mostar, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you have knowledge about any facts of looting committed by Vinko Skrobo soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the present time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the present time. I'm asking you about the time of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I believe the witness has answered the question, and now my learned friend is attempting to lead the witness to obtain a different answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Prosecutor, you have to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I have already rephrased my question. I asked him about the facts of looting, and if he knew -- if he had knowledge at the time when he was a soldier. I'm not asking the present time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the question has been asked and has been answered. This witness has no knowledge presently of anything that occurred in this regard when he was in Bosnia, in Mostar, in 1993. He answered the question. It's unfortunate that the answer was not that as sought by the Prosecutor, but it's an answer, and I don't believe it's proper to keep this line of questioning going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness said that at the present time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We could not understand what this means. It could be interpreted in several ways. So, Mr. Prosecutor, would you please clear it up for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, you just told that at a time present, no. But I'm not asking you about the present time. I'm just asking you if you had any knowledge about the facts of looting committed by Vinko Skrobo soldiers.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is -- sorry, what I didn't understand was did you mean in the beginning? Because in my eyes, we are still at the first time we went to Mostar. Or did you mean during the whole war when I was to Mostar? That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I was clear-cut in my second question: During the war when you were serving in the Vinko Skrobo unit. We are not talking about the initial stage of your serving in the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I just say something? This is a propos of what I said yesterday, Mr. Poriouvaev. Sometimes you asked this witness to deal chronologically, and then other times your questions are more general. The witness is trying - and I think doing it well - to deal with his first stay with the Vinko Skrobo unit in Mostar, and I think he was injured, he left for a while, and then he came back. So if we allow him to deal with it in two tranches - his first stay, the injury, going away, and then the coming back - probably we will get a much clearer picture, and then you can generalise at the end. It's a suggestion. He seems to like doing it that way, this witness. He's put some precision in his answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just asking some questions about a general character, not specifying the date, and that's why maybe my questions seem too general to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness Knudsen, just after Judge Clark's remarks and my explanation, could you give answer to this question?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a question. Your Honour, can I go to the toilet just for one minute? Seriously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will break for five minutes. --- Break taken at 10.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before you start, Mr. Prosecutor, I would like to say that I did not realise that when I said something about the oral motions made by Defence counsel, we were still in the private session. So we don't need this part to be in the private session, so this part of the confidentiality should be lifted as if it was delivered in the open session. Thank you. You may continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So, Mr. Knudsen, while asking you about beatings, lootings, I meant the whole period you were within Vinko Skrobo unit, which actually was not very long.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would say no, in a sense. I mean, we didn't see people running around looting. The deal is we were foreigners together. We go to the front line, you take your shift, you go back. And basically, because you did not speak the Croatian language, you stick together with these guys, and you actually don't have a lot of contact with the Croats. If we wanted something or needed something, we would go to Stela at the base unit and talk to Alan and he would translate. And that was mostly how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: All right. My next question will be: Did you participate in any military operations undertaken on the Bulevar area?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did that on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: 17th of what?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: September.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you informed of the forthcoming operation beforehand?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were informed the day before. We were on the front line or confrontation line, and a guy came to us on our shift, as I recall, named Damir, and talked to a us in a way, pidgin English. And are you ready for action tomorrow? We said, of course, we are ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Excuse me. Name of this guy?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Damir. I said of course we were ready, but we were not quite sure if something was about to happen. So we went home, you know, took our shift, got back, and were told that we were supposed to meet next day at the line at 9.00 p.m., and we did that. Do you want me to go further?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. That's why I'm --

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the line next day. The ammo guy was making our equipment ready when we got there. And Stela came there with Alan, and nobody at that time really knew what was going to happen. There was no - what you call it - plan of attack. There was no target being pointed at that time, present time. And then Stela came out and -- with this guy Alan, telling us, you know, we're going to take two buildings at the front line, and we were supposed to go first. There would be heavy artillery shelling from our side against the Muslim side. As we were told, it was going to be about 2.000 shelling, grenades. We didn't know how many. A couple, few hundred, I guess. And basically, that ammo guy, one guy from the ammo, and we would have prisoners in front of us as a shield. And he thought that was funny, you know, and he laughed at that. The deal, though, was these prisoners were supposed to make wooden guns. And they were actually sitting the night before making these guns at the base because we saw them as our apartment was about 800, 900 metres maybe away from Stela's. Not far. And we always walked this road to our house, you know, and they would sit outside making these wooden guns. And we came to the front line, and the attack was about to go off. A tank moving up, a T55, it's taken down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to stop at this point.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And we should clarify some more details about the initial stage of the operation. Did they told -- tell you which buildings should be reached during that operation? I mean the buildings on the opposite side of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told that we had a target, and our target were two buildings just the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you mean buildings that were indicated by you in the picture with number "5" and "6"?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time did the operation start on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was supposed to take off at 9.00 when we arrived, but I think it was about 11.00, something like that, when we took off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Where were you waiting for the beginning of the operation?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in bunkers. What I mean "bunkers," waiting inside, the building was built up with sand sacks from inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Which building?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white building, the dentist building, medical.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The medical building?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, position 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Position 1 as indicated in the pictures, position 1. Were prisoners with wooden rifles in the same building before the attack?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. They were in the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you actually see those, let's say, wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What did they look like?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like a wooden rifle. I mean, it was not what you call a good copy, if that's what you mean, but they looked like -- they were supposed to look like Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But did you see them at close range?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I did, because the prisoners were sitting close by, 1 or 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: In what uniform were prisoners dressed?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had civilian clothes at first, but when we were supposed to move out, they got this, you call it military jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What kind of jacket? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And who was the man who gave the order just to start the attack, to start the attack?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a guy in the bunker, a Croatian guy, and I'm not sure of his name. Everything is moving fast, and some guys said, "All right. We go out now." So we went outside and lined up behind the building, the prisoners first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back now to Exhibit 14.5. This is the same area but a little bit bigger. P14.5?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean P14.5?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So I would like you to mark the locations where you were waiting for the beginning of the attack with number "1"?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So, okay. Let's go on. So you left this building, and what did you see outside, first of all?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: As soon as you left the building, what was happening on the confrontation line at that time? You were inside of the building.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Outside, what was happening?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there has been a lot of shelling at first, but it was quiet outside now. And so we just lined up here behind the building, the prisoners going first, and then you ran here, beside the building, and in this direction here, and was pinned down behind this small wall up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you just show with a marker the direction you were moving?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And with an arrow in the end of the line, please.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was there a tank present at that time during the attack? Did you see --

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see the tank at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tent?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Tank?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank? Yeah, sorry. Yeah, because the tank was moving up first. Normally we had sandbags in this direction here, built over, but they has been removed the day before, and the tank move out about this position and started firing over here. At that time, we were sitting in here, you know, could see it come by, see it shoot or hear it shoot, and then it pull back. And then we got out here, this direction, and lying here, you know. And we were lying here, the tank moved up here and stopped here, right here, and started pointing the gun this way and everybody's, like, yelling because it's a pressure, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I suggest that you should mark with number "2" the place where the tank was standing and shooting the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last time or the first time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: First and second time.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Then it may be numbers "2" and "3."

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, explain.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably a bit difficult to see. What I mean is this: Where it moved, at the first time, because he was supposed to take out a bunker, this bunker we had at the corner here, and pull back, you know. And the second time he moved from here because at that time there was a lot of shooting, incoming fire, also with RPGs, rocket-propelled grenade launcher. He did not -- he was a bit afraid to move out at that time, and then he pulled back because his - what do you call it - telescope, was hit by a bullet, it was smashed, he couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. But just to make it clear, you should perhaps just mark with your fingers, "2" and "3" -- "3" and "4" now, at the end of the arrow -- of each arrow, "3," the initial, first movement of the tank and "4," the second one, when it returned and kept on moving.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me it's 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Knudsen, let's now return to prisoners with wooden rifles. By the way, was the Danish guy together with you during the attack?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was with me. He was lying -- I guess we got down there. I think there was about two guys in between me and him, and we had a German guy lying in the rear behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. So I suggest that you should take black colour, marker, because we have too much green light. I would ask you now to return to the way the prisoners with wooden rifles were moving and the group of soldiers, including you, the other Danish guy, and other foreigners, were moving towards the enemy position. You started doing it with a green light. Would you make it in a black colour from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The green one, because this is where we went in -- what you call in a row. And when we got out here, prisoners started running over here and got over there. And we were spread out and was lying exactly behind this wall down here. The time, I'm not quite sure. Maybe 15, 20 minutes. And I make this arrow because we couldn't get through, and we were to withdraw. Got back. There was a door here; prisoner kicked it out. So we moved in under cover. Some guys gave us covering fire. Moved in, and then returned to the yard here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Let's stop here. Let's return to the prisoners with the wooden rifles. Were they running in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were running in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: What was the distance between you and prisoners, in your estimation approximately?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Estimating, I would say 8, 8, 10 metres, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: In what position were they wearing their rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this, in front of them. They were ordered to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And so take the black marker again and show the direction the prisoners moved after the detonation.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And just explain the situation for the record.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation was that we were supposed to get down here behind the small wall; I guess it's about 1 metre high. And the prisoner was supposed to run -- it was an order they received to keep on moving forward against Muslim lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was there any commander on the spot who was controlling your actions and giving further commands while you were moving towards the Bosnian position?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not while we were moving, but we stopped moving because, like I said, we got pinned down here. The plan was to get this -- I'll point it out. The bunker system out here that had a machine-gun, and the plan was to get this bunker put out of the game. And after that, we were supposed to move in, you know, ducking down here. But we didn't get the bunker, and this guy in this bunker started shooting all the time, so we couldn't get out. The guy lying on my right side, which I believe was a commander or an officer of some kind, took an RPG, rocket-propelled grenade launcher, and fired, I think, three rounds against the bunker but didn't hit it. And after that, he gave the order we were supposed to move back because we couldn't get through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see -- did you see what happened to the prisoners with the wooden rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them fall down. Like, I can say I'm not sure they got killed or hit. I can only say three of them got down here outside the wall, at this piece, and you have one guy running over, reached the corner of the building. And we talked about it later because everybody was thinking that the guys was ducking down there as being killed, you know. I would say that we didn't see them get killed. We saw them fall down to the ground. And this guy kept running. He reached over here, and a grenade came down, I can show you where, about this position, so none of us were quite sure if he was dead or alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. But was the attack successful?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you reach the Muslim positions?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So how did you get wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back to behind the building here, gathering up troops from other units. Nobody really knew what was going to happen next. So I guess some guy, this Curly guy, who was with us behind the wall, gave the orders to move back, to get to position 1, which is this position here, and said to be on the lookout because the Muslims may - what do you call it - attack us, so he was going to say it was going to be a mistake. So I got there, and I was just looking a bit outside because the small mirror normally I was looking in was gone, so I put my head out a bit and snipers started shooting, and I tried to look at the position, and then a grenade came down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Would you indicate more or less the place where you were found by the grenade.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, I'll just point it out. Here in the middle, on the outside of the building, we had these sand sacks built up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were you taken to hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken to the hospital in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How long did you stay in hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any other units involved on that operation on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our units were, and we were told that brigade was being drawn from Livno to support us in the attack, and these guys were supposed to get out -- to move in these two directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Croatian guy, Alan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. You may take away now this exhibit from the ELMO, and I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit P606.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: These annotated P14.5 will be given the ID number P14.5/8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please have a look -- take a look at the original version of the document.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Is this your document?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was it given by the hospital authorities to you?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. And was it attached to your witness statement during the interview?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So, Mr. Knudsen, as follows from your witness statement and previous testimony, after the wounding, you left Mostar for some period of time for Denmark?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: When did you return to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about a couple of weeks later, a month. I don't remember exactly, but -- you couldn't just stay back in Denmark. I got back to Denmark, but you can't really talk to anybody about it, so the best thing to do was going to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Is it the situation when you returned to Mr. Barbic for the document to get to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went -- I went back to Zagreb, and Barbic always told us that if we needed anything, we could always contact him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did he give you a telephone number?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he gave me a telephone number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had his private number. We had the number to the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you again returned to Mostar. Were you allowed to keep on serving in that unit, in Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was allowed to. I found out I had been on the payroll as well, even since I was gone, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: How long did you stay with the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for long. Stayed a couple of weeks. Then we headed out, visited some other foreigners in Tomislavgrad. And then when we were sitting there in Tomislavgrad --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Don't hurry, please. Don't hurry.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sitting there, a Croatian guy who spoke fluent German, his name was Swapo. The Croats called him Pivo, which means "Beard". He came in and sat with the other foreigners and said he was on a lookout for new guys for a new platoon being built up in Ljubuski and anybody was interested in joining up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you join that platoon?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We joined that platoon, yeah, because he said to us it's going to be -- do not go to front line any more. This is a unit specifically for actions behind lines. And instead of 250 Deutschemarks, we would get 500 Deutschemarks, new uniform, new weapon. So it was at that time for us seemed as a pretty good offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You are saying "we," "us." Whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the Danish guy who went there with me. We had another German guy, which I do not recall. He just came down with us and checked Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Stop there, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The name should be redacted from the minutes now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came down to this unit and found out that the Canadian guy who was with us in Mostar was there as well. Other German guy which we had been to Orasje with came there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the unit you joined?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zeljko Bosnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who was in command of that unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a guy named Mario Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you know him before?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who was Mario Milicevic's commander?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean upper command?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, upper commander.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told it was Tuta. At that point, it was -- everybody would speak open, freely about what was happening, who was in charge. Good example would be we were supposed to have new American uniforms, and we were told that Tuta was in Zagreb at the moment negotiating to get these things down to us because we were not supposed to have Kalashnikov. We were supposed to have M-16s instead, as he felt it was a better weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you get any document confirming your membership in that unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit Number P241.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: We will take a look at this Croatian version. Is this your document?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who signed it?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see him sign the document?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, would you please tell us what this document is about. It has to be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Oh, right. Oh, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: This document issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you put it on the ELMO, if it's not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It is not under the seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please, Witness, perhaps you can inform the Trial Chamber of the date the document was issued.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's dated the 5th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't speak the Croatian language, read it at that time. I can see now what it means in English. But at that time, it was like a card that you are part of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And who is the person who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Mario Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see any stamp on the document just next to the signature on the original version?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now, Usher, I would like Witness Knudsen to be shown Exhibit Number 704. Page 22 of the English version. English version. I'm sorry, but I gave the list of exhibits to be used well beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Page 22 of the English version. Page 22. Is it page 22?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Did you find it? Please, Mr. Knudsen, take a look at this page --

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: -- the document, and read it. If you see any names that ring bells to you in this list?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first two names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Milicevic and Davor Rapic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Their military ranks?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I can see now, I didn't know their military ranks at that time except that -- but they were a major, a lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please go down with this list. Do you see any other names?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the foreign names.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see any other names familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see Markos Bardo, Stephan Rays, Alexander Nightline.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Don't hurry, please.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Kai Lutke, which I can't spell, and Tomas Franc-Kunst, [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Stop. Again, we should redact this name. Do you see your own name on this list?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 26, Allan Knudsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And number 27, without giving the name?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Knudsen, did you inform Stela, your former commander, that you were about to leave his unit for some different unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, not really. It went like this: We went, like I said, to Tomislavgrad, and in fact we did go directly from Tomislavgrad, because we drove with this guy, Pivo, down to the brigade immediately to check it out. And in a sense, you can say we stayed there and in time to come, we picked up our things in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you learn about the reaction with the, let's say, unauthorized to leave the unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say exactly. Everybody knew Stela at the time. And we talked to a Canadian guy and asked - what would you call it - tell us we should wait out a bit and pick our things up because Stela is not going to like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was there any difference between Zeljko Bosnjak unit and Vinko Skrobo unit in terms of organisational -- organisational, let's say, service, military service?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told from this guy let's - call him Pivo, because it was a name we used about him - this unit was only built for - what you call it - action behind lines. We were not supposed to be frontline service any more, so it was built for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any prisoners in this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had prisoners working as well. There was about three or four of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what was the attitude of soldiers to these prisoners? How did they treat you?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say that -- there was a big difference in what we seen in Mostar from this, because like I told before, at Mostar we didn't actually see prisoners get beaten up or treaten [sic] badly in that sense, but here they used a lot of beaten up, torture. Example could be if they were drunk, they could pull these guys out and put a bottle on their head and go maybe 20 metres back and start shooting after the bottles, you know. You want me to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they had these - I'm going to call it - war trials, pull in one or two prisoners, you know, and do -- ask them about they had been a soldier in the BH army, you know, burn them with cigarettes, beat them with bats or chains, accusing them of being hard-core Muslims who wanted a fundamentalist state.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you participate in any actions undertaken by the Zeljko Bosnjak unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that, do you mean military actions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I mean military actions or military-related actions.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to ask you, do you mean against army of BH, or the Serbs, or do you mean generally?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I mean generally, first of all.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We ran into a few problems with Vojna Policija, the military police in Ljubuski. It was, I would say, the only action we have really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have read this witness's statements. This witness is getting ready to commence testimony concerning action with the military police, not the army of BH and not the JNA or the Serb army, but a purely -- an action, if it took place, which was purely outside this indictment. It would not be a war crime, even if it did occur, and it's irrelevant. The probative value is zero, as compared to any prejudicial value to a fair trial, and I object to any line of testimony about any alleged actions against the military police in Ljubuski. They are not the Muslim army, the BH army, nor the Serb army. It's completely irrelevant to this war crimes trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't know whether it's a military army or the police unit at this moment. And, Mr. Prosecutor, would you please clear up for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can explain my position. Ljubuski military police station was the place where Mr. Knudsen saw certain persons who were involved in that action. And those persons I indicated in our indictment, so it is relevant to some persons additional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, that begs the question. The question is: Was this an action against a warring faction, the BH army or the Serb army. And Mr. Prosecutor has not told you that. He skirted the question you asked him, and that is whether it was against the BH army, the Muslim army, or the JNA. If it wasn't either one of those, it's not a war crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, would you please be more specific on the questions you are going to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We would like to know something more about this incident. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who was in command of those actions in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand what exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Who was in command of your unit during your actions in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Mario Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see any other people, persons, of high rank in the area?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw in the area but not inside Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Ljubuski, not the MUP station.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, not the MUP. You mean police?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Police, yes. Military police, sorry.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem was, as we understood it, we were told that -- Milicevic told us himself it was like this mafioso thing about military police in Ljubuski having problems with Tuta. If I may jump a bit, because, you know, it seems like Tuta was in charge. We got that confirmed in a sense elsewhere. Because at the time, in the middle of this, we were sitting at a bar downtown, the Danish guy and me. And suddenly the streets were empty. And this guy who owned the bar, who had nothing to do with the unit or us, said -- didn't know who we were. He didn't know which unit we were in. So he said to us, "You got to get out very quickly now because there's big problems now." And he used the expression "Tuta's army" making big problems at the moment. So we had to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you see Tuta there?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Ljubuski, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially, I have to tell the story. It goes like this: We were in Tomislavgrad and -- the Danish guy and I. And when we came back, it was a few hours. Maybe one hour before that, a guy from our unit was shot and killed in a bar brawl by a guy from military police. And we came back, they sealed off the streets where we were, and I was ordered to go up and get my weapon and my gear because something's going to happen now. I got back to the base, took my rifle and rucksack. And I went down, and I was ordered stand by a checkpoint and block to the military police if they came this way. And so I did. And we asked what happened, and this guy told us a story, you know. And he said the military police were going to come at us, and now they wanted to find this guy who shot one of our guys. And they found him in a basement in a house where he has been hiding, and they took him to interrogation at the base. We knew that because we were not allowed in a few hours to be in the apartment where we lived because they were interrogating the guy in there. And we heard a couple of shots then, and we went in about an hour later and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, Your Honours, the witness has gone on now for nearly a page uninterrupted speaking about an action, if anything, which would have been a civil nature for a criminal court in the country of Croatia. And in fact, I have been informed that there were persons brought before the criminal court in Zagreb over this incident. This is not a war crime in any fashion. It has not been alleged as a war crime, and I object strongly to any further testimony concerning this non -- this incident which, if it happened, was not a war crime, has never been alleged to have been a war crime, and certainly does not show anything of any systematic nature concerning the allegations brought and levelled by the Prosecutor's office against Mr. Naletilic. That's my objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, we have to know something, some incident, that is related to the charges in the indictment and as well as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to the accused. And you have to lead us towards this direction rather than detract the main aims, the main purpose of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: We do not allege this accident as a war crime. In the beginning of my examination, I just told that my questions will go to some issues including superior authority. And now, I would like to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If so, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mr. Knudsen, to be precise, did you see Tuta on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Tuta later, then, on the day -- I would say the day after. What happened is that the military police was about to take action against us, and we were put in some trucks, all the troops from Milicevic's unit, and told we were supposed to attack all military police station in the area, outskirts of Ljubuski, because he wanted -- like Milicevic told us, Tuta wanted to show the military police that this was his town, not theirs. So we were put in trucks, and we took this police station and moved on. And we saw Tuta on one occasion, only one. But I know that one of the German guys talked to this guy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you talk to Tuta?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was looking, standing there. He was about -- as we were told, he was supposed to be the leader of the action of all the ATG units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did he have weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he had a Glock.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's what I wanted to hear from Mr. Knudsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And just -- maybe my final question will be: Did you ever see HV units in the area you were making your military service? First of all, in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw military cars from HV in front of Stela's headquarters. I didn't see military personnel that I could link with HV. I could only see the number plate on the cars holding there and saying "HV."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: That was my final question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Mr. Par, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Knudsen. I'm counsel Zelimir Par on the Defence team of the accused Vinko Martinovic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did not have his earphones on when I was introducing myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm one of the Defence team of Vinko Martinovic, and my name is Zelimir Par. Let us start with your arrival at the Vinko Skrobo unit. Could we perhaps specify the length of your stay in days. How many days passed since your arrival until your first departure? Is it from the 9th September to the 17th of September, or is that not correct? Could you specify, please.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We actually did get our papers on the 9th. I think it was one, two weeks before got the paper. This I can explain by what we were told when I got there. The Croats not really trusted us as foreigners because they had a lot of incidents of foreigners coming to Mostar and ran over to the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: My question is simpler, really: How many days did you actually spend in that unit?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With altogether, would you say -- don't exactly remember. It's a lot of years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. Let's try to deal with the first part of your stay. You mentioned this document dated the 9th of September, by which you were officially admitted into the unit. And you said yesterday, if I remember correctly, that it was signed personally by Vinko Martinovic in your presence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I should now like to ask that this document be put on the ELMO. It's the Prosecutor's Exhibit 594, and I would like to ask you to look at that signature again. At the same time, I will let you see another paper where Vinko Martinovic put his signature at my request yesterday, and I would like to ask you to compare these two signatures. I would also like to remind you that an uncontested signature of Vinko Martinovic exists in the detention unit because he, of course, had to sign a number of papers there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I must object, Your Honour. Mr. Knudsen is a fact witness. He is not an expert witness. It's not within his scope just to compare signatures and to make conclusions, which one is appropriate and which one belongs to a certain person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, this witness has already told us that your client signed that paper in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Mr. President. However, I should like to respond to the objection of Mr. Poriouvaev. What we are dealing with here is an obvious difference between signatures, and I don't think one needs to be an expert to tell the difference. That's why I wanted to show it to him. And my intention regarding this witness is to see whether he would perhaps withdraw his statement or, alternatively, explain his claim. If you don't object, I would like to show him the original signature, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Par, is your position that your instructions from your client are that he did not sign this document? Are those your instructions? Well, then put it to this witness that "My client's instructions are that he did not sign this document, and that is not his signature." And then we know exactly what the issues are, instead of asking him to look at signatures and then ask him to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Honourable Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, my client claims that the signature on the certificate that you marked yesterday -- you identified yesterday as his signature is not his signature. He provided me also with his original signature, with the intention that I show it to you to corroborate his claim. If you don't mind, I would like to let you see this other signature now and ask you a direct question: Do you still continue to maintain that this statement was signed in your presence? I hope that I've formulated my question well this time.

utterances.speaker: ALLAN ASBJORN KNUDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I still claim that. I can only say what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
